# Surface accuracy and data efficiency: DrivAerML Surface and HiLiftAeroML {#sec-surface}

```{python}
#| label: setup-surface
#| include: false
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from palette import *
import json, statistics
from pathlib import Path
RES = Path("..") / "results"
J = lambda p: json.load(open(RES / p))
mean = statistics.mean
pct = lambda r: f"{abs(1 - r) * 100:.0f}%"

# ISLA is the reference configuration (384 wide, 12 layers, 256 slices, cosine routing, fused kernel, 5e-4), scored by
# the fleet scorer and reduced in results/ref_surface_2026-09-23.json; the training-car ladder below 435 cars is the
# REF-BOARD re-run of the same rungs (results/refboard_ladder_2026-09-23.json); the baseline rows are the released
# GeoTransolver and Transolver lanes of the reporting protocol.
REF = J("ref_surface_2026-09-23.json")["summary"]
ref_seeds = lambda k, f="pressure_l2": REF[k]["fields"][f]["seeds"]
RB = J("refboard_ladder_2026-09-23.json"); RBS = RB["summary"]; RBX = RB["learning_curve_exponents"]
P2 = J("p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json")
def ladder_rung(n):
    gt = {"1e-3": RBS[f"gt256|n{n}"], "3e-3": RBS[f"gt256_lr3e3|n{n}"]}
    glab = min(gt, key=lambda k: gt[k]["mean"])
    return dict(isla=RBS[f"isla_r1|n{n}"]["seeds"], gt=gt[glab]["seeds"], gt_rate=glab, t=RBS[f"transolver256|n{n}"]["seeds"])
A = P2["arms"]
gt435 = {"1e-3": A["gt_unit_lr1e3"], "3e-3": A["gt_unit_lr3e3"]}
g435lab = min(gt435, key=lambda k: gt435[k]["pressure_mean"])
runs = lambda a: [v["pressure_l2"] for v in a["per_run"].values()]
CARS = {n: ladder_rung(n) for n in (27, 54, 109, 218)}
CARS[435] = dict(isla=ref_seeds("isla_r1|dr435"), gt=runs(gt435[g435lab]), gt_rate=g435lab, t=runs(A["transolver_unit_lr3e3"]))
car_ratio = {n: (mean(r["gt"]) / mean(r["isla"]), mean(r["t"]) / mean(r["isla"])) for n, r in CARS.items()}
# the parameter-matched GeoTransolver-512, the depth variant R2 and the rate control, all at 435 cars; step time and memory
# of every configuration at 200,000 tokens from the reference cost sweep
GT512 = ref_seeds("gt_w512|dr435"); R2 = ref_seeds("isla_r2|dr435"); R1_LR = ref_seeds("isla_r1_lr1e3|dr435")
CS = {r["arm"]: r for r in J("cost_sweep_ref_gb300_bf16_2026-09-22.json")["runs"] if r["tokens"] == 200000 and r["status"] == "ok"}
COST = {k: (statistics.median(CS[a]["step_ms"]), CS[a]["peak_allocated_gib"]) for k, a in
        (("isla", "isla_ref_r1_384x12_cos_fused"), ("r2", "isla_ref_r2_384x24_cos_fused"), ("gt", "geotransolver_256"),
         ("gt512", "geotransolver_512"), ("t", "transolver_256"))}

# HiLiftAeroML: the case ladder, the geometry ladder and the fixed-angle split
F19 = J("p200k_fleet_reduction_2026-09-19.json")["datasets"]
F20 = J("p200k_fleet_interim_2026-09-20.json")["datasets"]
F22 = J("p200k_fleet_reduction_2026-09-22.json")["datasets"]
def gt_best(d):
    """GeoTransolver at the better of its 1e-3 and 3e-3 pairs; the rate label is read from the arm names,
    and 'rate not recorded' is printed where the artifact holds a single GeoTransolver arm without one."""
    a = d["arms"]; cands = {k: a[k] for k in ("gt_unit", "gt_unit_lr3e3") if k in a and a[k].get("n_evaluated")}
    k = min(cands, key=lambda k: cands[k]["pressure_l2_mean"])
    if len(cands) == 2:
        lab = "3e-3" if k.endswith("lr3e3") else "1e-3"
    else:
        lab = "3e-3" if k.endswith("lr3e3") else "rate not recorded"
    return cands[k]["pressure_l2_seeds"], lab
def wing_rung(d, isla=None):
    """One HiLiftAeroML rung. `isla` given: the reference configuration's seeds (REF); absent: the rung's ISLA lane is
    the earlier protocol (192 wide, linear routing, 1e-3) and is labeled so wherever it is printed."""
    g, lab = gt_best(d)
    return dict(gt=g, gt_rate=lab, t=d["arms"]["transolver_unit"]["pressure_l2_seeds"],
                isla=isla if isla is not None else d["arms"]["isla"]["pressure_l2_seeds"], isla_ref=isla is not None)
import glob as _glob
def ref_lane_seeds(stem, f="pressure_l2"):
    """Seed means of a reference-configuration lane pair from the fleet scorer's per-case rows
    (results/campaigns_2026-09-22/ref/metrics/<run>/<run>/metrics.jsonl), seeds 42 and 43."""
    out = []
    for sd in (42, 43):
        fs = sorted(_glob.glob(str(RES / "campaigns_2026-09-22" / "ref" / "metrics" / f"{stem}_seed{sd}" / "**" / "metrics.jsonl"), recursive=True))
        rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open(fs[0]) if '"infer_step"' in l]
        out.append(mean(r["metrics"][f] for r in rows))
    return out
SL_W = J("scalelaw_2026-09-27.json")["configurations"]  # the SCALE-LAW wing grid at 100,000 cells (GeoTransolver-512 at 510 wings)
WINGS = {
 "35 training cases": wing_rung(F19["highlift_surface_super_scarce"], isla=ref_seeds("isla_r1|hl35")),
 "210 training cases": dict(wing_rung(F22["highlift_surface_scarce"], isla=ref_lane_seeds("ref_isla_r1_hl210")),
                            gt=ref_lane_seeds("ref_gt_w512_hl210"), gt_rate="GeoTransolver-512, 3e-3"),
 "510 training cases": dict(gt=SL_W["hilift|gt|w512|n510"]["pressure_l2_seeds"], gt_rate="GeoTransolver-512 at 100,000 cells, 3e-3",
                            t=None, isla=ref_lane_seeds("ref_isla_r1_hl510"), isla_ref=True),
 "4 training geometries": wing_rung(F20["highlift_surface_geometry_super_scarce"]),
 "21 training geometries": wing_rung(F22["highlift_surface_geometry_scarce"]),
 "126 geometries at 12°": wing_rung(F20["highlift_surface_single_aoa_12"]),
}
wing_ratio = {k: (mean(r["gt"]) / mean(r["isla"]), (mean(r["t"]) / mean(r["isla"])) if r["t"] else None) for k, r in WINGS.items()}
GT512_LADDER = {"35": mean(ref_seeds("gt_w512|hl35")) / mean(WINGS["35 training cases"]["isla"]),
                "210": wing_ratio["210 training cases"][0], "510": wing_ratio["510 training cases"][0]}
HP210 = J("hl210_percase_2026-09-27.json"); S210 = HP210["summary"]
EARLIER = "earlier protocol (192 wide, 1e-3)"
isla_lab = lambda r: "ISLA" if r["isla_ref"] else f"ISLA, {EARLIER}"
GT512_W = ref_seeds("gt_w512|hl35"); R2_W = ref_seeds("isla_r2|hl35"); R1_LR_W = ref_seeds("isla_r1_lr1e3|hl35")
PC = J("drivaer435_percase_2026-09-23.json")  # per-car anatomy of the 435-car standing (ISLA against GeoTransolver-512)
```

```{python}
#| label: para-surface-lede
#| output: asis
g27, g54, g109, g435 = (car_ratio[n][0] for n in (27, 54, 109, 435))
g512 = mean(GT512) / mean(CARS[435]["isla"])
w = wing_ratio
print(f"**On the DrivAerML Surface task ISLA leads GeoTransolver at its recipe width by {pct(g435)} at 435 training cars "
      f"(GeoTransolver-256 ÷ ISLA {g435:.2f}, both seeds agreeing) and from 109 cars up. It leads Transolver by {pct(car_ratio[435][1])}. "
      f"It is at parity with the parameter-matched GeoTransolver-512 (÷ ISLA {g512:.2f}), which costs {COST['gt512'][0] / COST['isla'][0]:.2f}x ISLA's "
      f"step time and {COST['gt512'][1] / COST['isla'][1]:.1f}x its memory. Below 109 cars GeoTransolver-256 leads, by {pct(g27)} at 27 "
      f"cars and {pct(g54)} at 54. On HiLiftAeroML the baselines lead ISLA on every rung. GeoTransolver leads by {pct(w['35 training cases'][0])} at 35 "
      f"training cases, by {pct(w['4 training geometries'][0])} at 4 training geometries, by {pct(w['126 geometries at 12°'][0])} on the fixed-angle "
      f"split, and by {pct(w['21 training geometries'][0])} at 21 training geometries, where the validation geometries are never seen. "
      f"Against the parameter-matched GeoTransolver-512 the wing deficit closes with training cases: GeoTransolver-512 ÷ ISLA "
      f"{GT512_LADDER['35']:.2f} / {GT512_LADDER['210']:.2f} / {GT512_LADDER['510']:.2f} at 35 / 210 / 510 wings.** The wing deficit is a "
      "small-data, recurring-geometry effect. It is within seed noise where the validation geometries are held out of a training set of a "
      "few tens of geometries. It does not move with the number of sampled cells, with ISLA's width or with its depth. The metric throughout is the area-weighted relative L2 error of surface "
      "pressure in float32 (@sec-metrics). Every ratio is baseline ÷ ISLA, and a value above one favors ISLA. The protocol is that of "
      "@sec-protocol: 200,000 sampled cells per case, 500 epochs, two seeds, each architecture at its own best learning rate. ISLA is the "
      f"reference configuration of @sec-using-config (384 wide, 12 layers, {CS['isla_ref_r1_384x12_cos_fused']['n_params'] / 1e6:.1f}M parameters, learning rate 5e-4). "
      f"GeoTransolver runs at its recipe width of 256 ({CS['geotransolver_256']['n_params'] / 1e6:.1f}M) and, where named, at 512 wide "
      f"({CS['geotransolver_512']['n_params'] / 1e6:.1f}M, the parameter match). Transolver runs at 256 wide ({CS['transolver_256']['n_params'] / 1e6:.1f}M). "
      "The 4-geometry, 21-geometry and fixed-angle rungs still carry ISLA lanes of the earlier protocol (192 wide, linear routing, "
      "1e-3) and are labeled so; the 35-, 210- and 510-case rungs are the reference configuration against GeoTransolver-512 "
      "(@sec-nb-ref-hl210-verdict, @sec-nb-ref-hl510-verdict).")
```

```{python}
      f"({seeds(r['isla'])}) below both GeoTransolver seeds ({seeds(r['gt'])}).** The lead is against GeoTransolver at its recipe width, "
      f"the configuration the reporting protocol trains at ({CS['geotransolver_256']['n_params'] / 1e6:.1f}M parameters against "
      f"ISLA's {CS['isla_ref_r1_384x12_cos_fused']['n_params'] / 1e6:.1f}M). ISLA trains beside it at {COST['isla'][0] / COST['gt'][0]:.2f}x "
      f"the step time and {COST['isla'][1] / COST['gt'][1]:.2f}x the memory (@sec-cost-sweep). Matched on parameters instead, GeoTransolver-512 "
      f"({CS['geotransolver_512']['n_params'] / 1e6:.1f}M) scores {mean(GT512):.4f} ({seeds(GT512)}). That is parity with ISLA "
      f"(÷ ISLA {g512:.2f}) at {COST['gt512'][0] / COST['isla'][0]:.2f}x ISLA's step time and {COST['gt512'][1] / COST['isla'][1]:.1f}x its memory. "
      f"The parity holds car by car: the per-car ratio runs from {PC['per_car_ratio_gt512_over_isla_r1']['p10']:.2f} to "
      f"{PC['per_car_ratio_gt512_over_isla_r1']['p90']:.2f} between the 10th and 90th percentiles, ISLA is the more accurate model on "
```

```{python}
def cell(v):
    return f"{mean(v):.4f} ({min(v):.4f}–{max(v):.4f})" if len(v) > 1 else f"{v[0]:.4f} (one seed)"
GIB_TO_GB = 1024 ** 3 / 1e9
isla435 = mean(r["isla"])
rows435 = [("**ISLA** (384 x 12, 5e-4)", "isla", r["isla"]), ("ISLA, 24 layers (384 x 24, 5e-4)", "r2", R2), ("ISLA at 1e-3 (rate control)", "isla", R1_LR),
           (f"GeoTransolver-256 ({r['gt_rate']}), the recipe width", "gt", r["gt"]), ("GeoTransolver-512 (3e-3), the parameter match", "gt512", GT512),
           ("Transolver-256 (3e-3)", "t", r["t"])]
out = "| configuration at 435 training cars | parameters | surface pressure error, mean (seed range) | ÷ ISLA | step [ms] | peak memory [GB] |\n|---|--:|---|--:|--:|--:|\n"
ARMN = {"isla": "isla_ref_r1_384x12_cos_fused", "r2": "isla_ref_r2_384x24_cos_fused", "gt": "geotransolver_256", "gt512": "geotransolver_512", "t": "transolver_256"}
for lab, ck, v in rows435:
    out += (f"| {lab} | {CS[ARMN[ck]]['n_params'] / 1e6:.1f}M | {cell(v)} | {mean(v) / isla435:.2f} | {COST[ck][0]:.0f} | "
            f"{COST[ck][1] * GIB_TO_GB:.0f} |\n")
print(out)
print(": The 435-car standing of the DrivAerML Surface task, every configuration at the reporting protocol (200,000 sampled cells per "
      "case, 500 epochs, two seeds, float32 on the 48 validation cars). The ratio is the row's error divided by ISLA's, so a value above "
      "one means ISLA is more accurate than that row. Step time and peak memory are the training step at 200,000 tokens on one GB300 in "
      "bf16 with a batch of one, from the reference cost sweep (@sec-cost-sweep), the same instrument for every row. How to read this: "
      "the two GeoTransolver rows differ in what is matched, the recipe width or the parameter count. ISLA leads the first and ties the "
      "second at lower cost. The 24-layer ISLA row is the depth variant the reference selection rejected. Data: "
```

### The anatomy of the cell-count gap {#sec-deficit-anatomy}

```{python}
#| label: para-anatomy-200k
#| output: asis
tenk = P2["tenk_reference"]
qv = J("quadvar_reduction_2026-09-17.json")["arms"]
r_ind10 = qv["gt_unit"]["unif"]["10000"] / qv["isla_ref"]["unif"]["10000"]
r_strat10 = qv["gt_unit"]["strat"]["10000"]["mean"] / qv["isla_ref"]["strat"]["10000"]["mean"]
r_ind40 = qv["gt_unit"]["unif"]["40000"] / qv["isla_ref"]["unif"]["40000"]
r435 = CARS[435]
isla192_200k = mean(runs(A["isla"])); g435_192 = mean(r435["gt"]) / isla192_200k
print(f"**Below 100,000 cells per case ISLA's error carries finite-sample noise in its slice integrals. At the reporting protocol that noise "
      f"is gone.** The term was measured on the lanes of the earlier protocol (ISLA 192 wide, 1e-3). The 10,000- and 40,000-cell draws below "
      f"were read from those lanes' 435-car checkpoints. The mechanism is the sampling draw, not the width: the reference "
      f"configuration shows the same count dependence in its biased-draw factor (@sec-robustness-density). Trained and scored at 10,000 cells "
      f"(a rung of the ladder, not a standing) GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA is {tenk['gt_unit'] / tenk['isla']:.2f}. At 200,000 cells, for the same "
      f"192-wide configuration, it is {g435_192:.3f}. Every model improves with the denser sample, and ISLA improves the most "
      f"({(1 - P2['verdict']['isla_200k_over_10k']) * 100:.0f}% against {(1 - mean(r435['gt']) / tenk['gt_unit']) * 100:.0f}% for GeoTransolver "
      f"and {(1 - mean(r435['t']) / tenk['transolver_unit']) * 100:.0f}% for Transolver). An independent draw of a car's surface at a small cell "
      "count is a noisy instrument. ISLA's slice states are measure-weighted means over the draw (@sec-isla-quadrature), so they inherit more "
      "of that noise than the baselines' unweighted aggregates. Two readings of the same 435-car checkpoints locate the noise. A stratified draw of "
      f"the same 10,000 cells (@sec-using-sampler), which keeps the inclusion law and spreads the cells evenly, moves GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA from "
      f"{r_ind10:.3f} to {r_strat10:.3f}. An independent 40,000-cell draw moves it to {r_ind40:.3f}. At 200,000 cells it is {g435_192:.3f}. "
      "For deployment the consequence is the recommendation of @sec-using-sampler: use the stratified draw, or more cells. The wing deficit "
      "below is a different mechanism, and the cell count does not touch it. Data: results/p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json (with its "
      "10,000-cell reference), results/quadvar_reduction_2026-09-17.json. Every number in this paragraph is the earlier protocol's.")
```

## HiLiftAeroML {#sec-data-efficiency}

### What is measured {#sec-de-setup}

HiLiftAeroML (@sec-datasets) holds 1,800 cases: 180 high-lift wing
geometries, each simulated at ten angles of attack from 4° to 22°. Three
ladders vary what the training set contains and how large it is. All of
them score on 180 validation cases with the same instrument.

- **The case ladder.** Nested random draws of 35 and 210 training cases
  from a 1,260-case pool, sharing one 180-case validation set
  (@sec-splits). The validation geometries recur in training at other
  angles. The 35-case draw contains 33 distinct geometries and no case at
  18°.
- **The geometry ladder.** 40 cases on 4 geometries and 210 cases on 21
  geometries, each at all ten angles, validated on 180 cases of 18
  geometries that appear in no training set.
- **The fixed-angle split.** 126 geometries at 12°, validated on 18
  held-out geometries at the same angle.

The protocol is that of @sec-protocol. GeoTransolver's better rate on the
wings is 3e-3 wherever both of its pairs exist. Transolver runs at 3e-3.
ISLA is the reference configuration (384 wide, 5e-4) on the 35-, 210- and
510-case rungs, where the baseline is the parameter-matched GeoTransolver-512
(at 510 wings its pair is the SCALE-LAW lane at 100,000 cells, a count at
which GeoTransolver's error is flat to 1%, @sec-nb-scalehl-verdict). On the
other three rungs the ISLA lane is still the earlier protocol's (192 wide,
linear routing, 1e-3), labeled so in every row, until its
reference-configuration re-run lands (@sec-program-status). On the 35-case
rung, where both exist, the reference configuration scores
`{python} f"{(1 - mean(WINGS['35 training cases']['isla']) / mean(F19['highlift_surface_super_scarce']['arms']['isla']['pressure_l2_seeds'])) * 100:.0f}%"`
below the earlier protocol's lane, so the labeled rows understate ISLA by
a few percent at most, not by the size of the baselines' lead.

```{python}

#|   The HiLiftAeroML rungs at the reporting protocol (200,000 cells per

#|   ISLA is the reference configuration on the case rungs (filled squares),
#|   against GeoTransolver-512 at 210 and 510 wings (the 510-wing pair is the

#|   three rows marked "earlier protocol" the ISLA lane is 192 wide at 1e-3
#|   (open square) and its reference re-run is in flight. How to read this:
#|   the baselines' lead is largest where the training set is small and its
#|   geometries recur in validation, closes with cases, and is within

#|   geometries; the rungs differ several-fold in absolute error, which is why

ROWS = [("35 training cases", "35 random training cases\n(geometries recur)"),

        ("21 training geometries", "21 training geometries, 210 cases\n(never-seen geometries)"),
        ("126 geometries at 12°", "126 geometries at a fixed 12°\n(18 held-out geometries)")]
```

```{python}
      f"geometries at ten angles against 35 cases on 33 geometries) costs ISLA {geo_cost:.1f}x (@tbl-hilift-ladder). The comparison changes "
      "the validation population as well as the training composition. It therefore supports a geometry-count reading and not the stronger "
      "statement that geometry count alone sets the error.")
```

```{python}
      "across angles. The two architectures find the same cases hard at both rungs (Spearman rank "
      f"correlation of the per-case errors {HP['spearman_isla_r1_gt512']:.2f} over {HP['n_cases']} validation cases on {HP['n_geometries']} "

      "moves no angle group by more than 4%, so depth does not buy the separated regime either. What GeoTransolver-512 has and ISLA does not "
      "is the absolute position of every cell (@sec-part-baseline); in the separated regime the pressure depends on where along the chord "
      "and span a cell sits more than on its local geometry. This is a location of the deficit at one rung, not its mechanism, and the 210-case twin says the location is "
      "not a fixed property of the regime (@sec-nb-hl35-percase, @sec-nb-ref-hl210-verdict). How much of the deficit is the fixed pose itself is quantified by the pose-prior diagnostic "
      "of @sec-pose-prior, which gives ISLA the dataset's axes as inputs, an input the book rejects: about half of the low-angle gap and a "
      "quarter of the high-angle widening, so the separated regime keeps the rest.")
```

## A second surface task: DeepJEB++ brackets {#sec-surface-deepjeb}

```{python}
#| label: setup-deepjeb
#| include: false
JB = J("deepjeb_2026-09-22.json"); JBS = JB["summary"]
JB_RUNGS = [("n256", 256, 500), ("n1024", 1024, 125), ("n4096", 4096, 32), ("full", 12451, 10)]
JB_FIELDS = [("von_mises", "von Mises stress"), ("displacement", "displacement")]
def jb_best(rung, f):
    """The GeoTransolver arm with the lowest mean on this rung and field, as the preregistration specifies."""
    cands = {a: JBS[f"{a}|{rung}"] for a in ("gt512", "gt512_lr3e3", "gt256") if f"{a}|{rung}" in JBS}
    a = min(cands, key=lambda a: cands[a]["fields"][f]["mean"]); return a, cands[a]
JB_NAME = {"gt512": "GeoTransolver-512 (1e-3)", "gt512_lr3e3": "GeoTransolver-512 (3e-3)", "gt256": "GeoTransolver-256 (1e-3)"}
jb_ratio = {(rung, f): jb_best(rung, f)[1]["fields"][f]["mean"] / JBS[f"isla_r1|{rung}"]["fields"][f]["mean"]
            for rung, _, _ in JB_RUNGS for f, _ in JB_FIELDS}
```

```{python}
#| label: para-deepjeb-lede
#| output: asis
vm = [jb_ratio[(r, "von_mises")] for r, _, _ in JB_RUNGS]; dp = [jb_ratio[(r, "displacement")] for r, _, _ in JB_RUNGS]
print(f"**On DeepJEB++, a surface task whose global vector is a load direction rather than a freestream, ISLA leads or ties the best "
      f"GeoTransolver arm at every rung of an equal-step ladder on both fields: GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA {min(vm):.2f} to {max(vm):.2f} on von "
      f"Mises stress and {min(dp):.2f} to {max(dp):.2f} on displacement over 256 to 12,451 training brackets.** DeepJEB++ "
      "(@sec-datasets-beyond-aero) is a family of generated jet-engine brackets. Each is solved by linear static finite elements under four "
      "load cases applied at the lug bore with the bolt holes clamped: three force directions and a torque about the lug axis. The "
      "surface mesh carries the fixed and loaded labels and the traction as boundary scalars. The load direction enters ISLA as the one "
      "global vector, and a force/torque one-hot enters as two global scalars (a moment axis is a pseudovector, so the model is told when the "
      "vector is an axis). The targets are von Mises stress and displacement at the surface cells. The test set is 1,385 held-out "
      "brackets under all four loads (5,540 files), scored in float32 over every surface cell. The ladder holds the optimizer-step "
      "budget fixed at about 130,000 steps while the training set grows (500, 125, 32 and 10 epochs at 256, 1,024, 4,096 and 12,451 "
      "brackets). It is therefore an equal-compute comparison at each rung and not a learning curve. Both architectures are flat above 1,024 "
      "brackets at this budget, which says the models are step-limited there, and the data exponent is not readable from it "
      "(@sec-nb-deepjeb-prereg; the equal-epoch companion at the full rung is in flight, @sec-program-status).")
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-deepjeb-surface
#| output: asis
def jbcell(g, f):
    s = g["fields"][f]["seeds"]
    return f"{g['fields'][f]['mean']:.3f}" + (" (one seed)" if len(s) == 1 else "")
out = "| training brackets (epochs) | ISLA: von Mises / displacement | best GeoTransolver arm | its von Mises / displacement | GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA |\n|---:|---|---|---|---:|\n"
for rung, n, ep in JB_RUNGS:
    i = JBS[f"isla_r1|{rung}"]
    a_vm, g_vm = jb_best(rung, "von_mises"); a_dp, g_dp = jb_best(rung, "displacement")
    arm = JB_NAME[a_vm] if a_vm == a_dp else f"{JB_NAME[a_vm]} / {JB_NAME[a_dp]}"
    out += (f"| {n:,} ({ep}) | {jbcell(i, 'von_mises')} / {jbcell(i, 'displacement')} | {arm} | {jbcell(g_vm, 'von_mises')} / "
            f"{jbcell(g_dp, 'displacement')} | {jb_ratio[(rung, 'von_mises')]:.2f} / {jb_ratio[(rung, 'displacement')]:.2f} |\n")
print(out)
print(": DeepJEB++ at equal optimizer steps (about 130,000; epochs in parentheses): relative L2 of von Mises stress and displacement over "
      "every surface cell, mean over the 5,540 clean test files, float32, two seeds unless marked. ISLA is the reference configuration "
      "(384 x 12, 5e-4, the load direction as the global vector); the GeoTransolver column is the arm with the lowest mean on that rung "
      "and field, as preregistered, among GeoTransolver-512 at 1e-3 and 3e-3 and GeoTransolver-256 at 1e-3 where they were run. How to read "
      "this: the ratio is GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA, above one favoring ISLA. The rows are equal-compute standings, not a learning curve, and the "
      "flatness above 1,024 brackets is the step budget. Data: results/deepjeb_2026-09-22.json; the notebook table of the same numbers is "
      "@tbl-deepjeb-equalstep. {#tbl-deepjeb-surface}")
```


## Limits of these standings {#sec-de-limits}


- **The ladders are data-efficiency measurements, not scaling laws.** Their
  rungs span the range of data every production CFD dataset in this program
  occupies. On the DrivAerML Surface task the flattening has a measured
  cause: a shared floor of about 0.040 that both architectures reach given
  width and depth, with the cell count flat above 100,000
  (@sec-shared-floor). On the wings the flattening is not attributed.
- **Every number is in-distribution and a validation-set figure.** The
  validation cases share the training design. Checkpoints are final-epoch
  with no selection, but the validation set entered more than one decision:
  each architecture's learning rate on the full split (@sec-lr-protocol),
  the baselines' rate per rung, the design of the ablations and the choice
  of what to present. No HiLiftAeroML split remains that can confirm the
  numbers independently of the program's own history. The sealed test
  splits were spent on regime extrapolation and the deflection split, which
  between them read every one of the 180 geometries
  (results/hilift_exposure_ledger_2026-09-08.json). Every remaining test
  split is therefore held out per checkpoint, since no model trained on it,
  but it is not a program-level confirmation. An independent confirmation
  needs geometries no part of the program has scored, which on HiLiftAeroML
  means a prospective dataset.
- **Seeds do not measure the choice of training cases.** Every seed at a
  rung trains on the same curated subset, so seed ranges measure
  initialization. The draw intervals of @sec-de-controls are the
  uncertainty to read.
- **The in-distribution lead is against GeoTransolver at its recipe width,
  on one dataset, from 109 cars up. No mechanism for it is claimed.** At
  matched parameters (GeoTransolver-512) the two are at parity at 435 cars.
  What ISLA buys at full data is therefore cost, not accuracy: the same
  error at the parameter match's 0.85x step time and half its memory
  (@tbl-scoreboard-435). Below 109 cars GeoTransolver-256 leads. On the
  wings both baselines lead on every rung, and the reference configuration,
  the depth variant, the rate control and GeoTransolver-512 all leave that
  ordering where it is. What ISLA buys elsewhere is stated with its scope
  where it is measured: exact pose covariance (@sec-pose-contract), weak
  dependence on the law the training sample is drawn by
  (@sec-training-law), slice territories that stay put under a change of
  draw (@sec-territories), the interior leads on two datasets
  (@sec-interior) and the memory frontier (@sec-cost-sweep). The mechanism
  of the wing deficit, the mesher pattern where validation geometries recur
  in training, is an open question (@sec-open-questions).
- **Regime extrapolation is unmeasured for ISLA.** Across an angle-of-attack
  or stall boundary the architectures measured lose about an order of
  magnitude in error. The notebook carries the degradation ratios
  (@sec-nb-hl-sealed-test), and this chapter makes no cross-regime claim.
